h1: Lighting, Fans & Outlets in South Florida
intro: Not every call is a panel or a rebuild. Recessed lighting, a ceiling fan over the patio, new outlets where the extension cords have taken over, a smart switch that outsmarted its last installer. Our licensed crew handles the everyday work with the same care as the big jobs.

definition.heading: What our everyday electrical service covers
definition.body: Indoor and outdoor lighting, recessed cans and LED upgrades, ceiling fans, outlets and switches, GFCI protection, dimmers, and smart home devices. Small jobs still ride on the wiring behind the wall, which is why a licensed electrician is worth having for them.

symptoms.title: Extension cords doing a wall's job
symptoms.body: The room needs more outlets. Cords across a floor are a trip hazard and a fire risk that a few properly wired outlets retire for good.

symptoms.title: Rooms the builder left too dark
symptoms.body: Recessed cans, pendants, or under-cabinet light change how a room works. We lay it out, wire it, and patch in cleanly.

symptoms.title: A ceiling fan that wobbles, hums, or is not there yet
symptoms.body: Fans need a rated box and correct wiring, not a hook and hope. We hang them so they run smooth and quiet.

symptoms.title: Switches, dimmers, and smart devices acting up
symptoms.body: Buzzing dimmers, three-way switches wired wrong, a smart switch that refuses to behave. We sort out the wiring behind the symptom.

process.title: Tell us the list

localSections.heading: Small electrical work, done like the big jobs
localSections.body: Patio fans, landscape lighting, and outdoor outlets do heavy duty in heat, humidity, and salt air, and corrosion finds casual work quickly. We use rated fixtures, weather-resistant devices, and in-use covers that meet code.

localSections.heading: Older wiring behind new devices
localSections.body: A smart switch is only as reliable as the wiring behind it, and plenty of South Florida homes still run on wiring from their first owner. Missing grounds, crowded boxes, and tired connections turn up mid-job. We never bury a problem behind a new plate.

guide.title: The honest guide to everyday electrical work

sections.heading: Why small jobs still deserve a licensed hand
sections.body: Most electrical fires start at connections, and connections are exactly what lighting, fan, and outlet work is made of. A fixture on the wrong box, or an outlet back-stabbed instead of properly terminated, can sit quietly for years before it becomes a problem. We do the small work to the same standard as a service rebuild.

sections.heading: Lighting and fans that actually fit the room
sections.body: Good lighting is layout first: where the cans go, what the dimmer controls, how warm the light runs. We plan it before cutting a hole. Fans have their own rules, a fan-rated box that carries weight and motion, correct switch wiring, and damp or wet rated models anywhere weather reaches.

sections.heading: Outlets, GFCI, and the smart home layer
sections.body: Code requires GFCI protection where water lives: kitchens, bathrooms, garages, laundry, and outdoors. If your home predates those rules, adding it is one of the cheapest safety upgrades there is. Smart switches add a wrinkle, since many need a neutral wire that older boxes never carried.

faqs.question: Do you really take small jobs?
faqs.answer: Yes. Plenty of customers meet us on a small job first. All we ask is the chance to group your list into one visit, because a single planned trip is the economical way to handle small work.

faqs.question: Can you install a ceiling fan where there is only a light now?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. The existing box almost never rates for a fan, so we swap in a fan-rated box and sort the switching so the fan and light control the way you want.

faqs.question: Why does my new smart switch not work in my older home?
faqs.answer: Usually because the switch box has no neutral wire, which many smart switches need to stay powered. We check what your boxes actually carry and tell you which devices will work as-is.

faqs.question: Do lighting or outlet jobs need a permit?
faqs.answer: Swapping a fixture or replacing a device like for like generally does not. New circuits and new outlet locations generally do. We tell you which yours is, and pull the permit where one applies.
